Definition
[equicontinuous family]

Source: petersen:page-0415 ↗ def:pet-ch11-convergence-of-maps Call a family $f_k:X_k\to Y_k$ equicontinuous when, for every $\varepsilon >0$ and $x_k\in X_k$ there is $\delta >0$ with $f_k(B(x_k,\delta ))\subset B(f_k(x_k),\varepsilon )$ for all $k$. Uniformly Lipschitz families are equicontinuous.
